title: Section 12 Limitation Act — Time for copies

content.overview: Section 12 of the Limitation Act, 1963 is a computation rule. In computing limitation for any suit, appeal or application, the day from which the period is to be reckoned is excluded. For an appeal, an application for leave to appeal, a revision, or a review, the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the decree, sentence or order is also excluded, and the day on which the judgment complained of was pronounced is excluded. The time requisite for obtaining a copy of the judgment on which the decree or order is founded is excluded as well. Time taken to obtain a copy is the time requisite, not every day the party later chooses to wait.
content.study: Exclude the start day in every computation. Exclude copy time only for appeal, leave, revision and review. Do not exclude copy time from a suit unless another section says so.

learningObjectives: Exclude the reckoning day under section 12(1).
Exclude requisite copy time for appeal, revision and review.
Keep copy-time exclusion off ordinary suits.
enhancement.definition: Section 12 excludes the day from which limitation is reckoned and, for appeal, revision and review, the time requisite for obtaining the necessary copy.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Section 12 is exclusion in computation, not condonation. The party does not need sufficient cause for the days the section excludes.
enhancement.statutoryFramework: Limitation Act, 1963, section 12. Section 5 is a different power.
essentialIngredients: Period being computed for a suit, appeal or application
For appeal, leave, revision or review, judgment day excluded
Time requisite for the decree, sentence or order copy excluded
Time requisite for the judgment copy excluded
No extra delay after the copy was ready
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 12(1) applies to suits as well as appeals and applications, but only for the day from which the period is to be reckoned. Section 12(2) is narrower. It applies to an appeal, an application for leave to appeal, a revision, and a review of a judgment. It excludes the day the judgment was pronounced and the time requisite for obtaining a copy of the decree, sentence or order appealed from or sought to be revised or reviewed. Section 12(3) excludes the time requisite for a copy of the judgment on which that decree or order is founded. Section 12(4) deals with a copy served without the party's application and is read before adding waiting time. The exclusion is the time requisite, which is the time required to obtain the copy, not a later period of inaction.
examples: A three-year suit period starts on 1 March. That day is excluded under section 12(1). Copy time is not excluded from the suit.
An appeal is filed after the period, but the days taken to obtain the decree copy are excluded under section 12(2).
The copy was ready and the party waited a further month. That further month is not time requisite under section 12.
enhancement.problemApplication: Exclude the start day. Add copy time only if the proceeding is an appeal, leave application, revision or review, and only for the time requisite. Send any remaining delay to section 5 if that section applies.
distinctions: Start-day exclusion for suits vs copy-time exclusion

Copy time is excluded for appeal, leave, revision and review.
